featured.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程创作者、前 Roblox/Reddit 产品负责人
featured.summaryEn: The biggest AI story this week is OpenAI gating GPT-5.6 Sol to ~20 pre-approved companies, and Peter Yang laid out the uncomfortable chain: we publish frontier models, they get distilled into cheap open-source ones, US companies adopt those because they're good enough and far cheaper, and then we start gating frontier access. His implied punchline: this just makes US companies innovate less and open source more attractive. His more grounded take: money has shifted to services (with some software bundled), not pure…
featured.insightZh: 这周 AI 圈最大的话题是 OpenAI 发布 GPT-5.6 Sol 却把访问权限收窄到约 20 家预批准公司，Peter Yang 顺着这条逻辑链发了一连串犀利质问：我们发布前沿模型 → 它们被蒸馏成廉价开源模型 → 美国公司因为「够用且便宜得多」转去用开源模型 → 然后我们开始给前沿模型设访问门槛。他的潜台词是：这套玩法最终只会让美国公司创新更少、让开源模型更有吸引力。另一条更接地气的观察是，钱正在从「软件」转向「服务+少量软件捆绑」——人们要的是结果，不是工具，纯软件公司很难做到比「Codex/Claude Code + 一堆个人 skill 和 agent」更有价值。他还顺手给 Claude Code 提了几条产品建议：恢复工作中途插话引导对话的能力、默认开启全线程的移动端远程控制、支持 cmd+键 的线程快捷切换。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie gave a clear bull take on the new model: "GPT-5.6 is real and looks very strong. Going to be very strong for knowledge worker tasks that require heavy tool use and long running agents doing work. We're not hitting any walls in AI progress right now." In the ongoing "have we plateaued" debate, he's firmly on the not-even-close side.
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 对 GPT-5.6 给出了明确的乐观判断：「GPT-5.6 是真的，而且看起来非常强。对那些需要重度工具调用和长时间运行 agent 干活的知识工作者任务会非常强。我们现在在 AI 进展上没撞到任何墙。」在「AI 是否到顶」的辩论里，他站在「还远没到」这一边。

featured.title: Ep: Noam Brown 谈为什么传统基准测试在现代 AI 上失效
featured.summaryEn: A modern model's capability is a function of how much money you pour into it — yet everyone still evaluates models with a single-number benchmark grid that doesn't control for test-time compute. The whole evaluation paradigm is broken at the root. No Priors hosts OpenAI research scientist Noam Brown, one of the godfathers of AI reasoning. His core argument targets the "benchmark grid" everyone publishes with new models (benchmarks on the x-axis, model scores on the y-axis). The problem: it reduces a model's performance to a single number per benchmark while ignoring how much test-time compute went into each question. On paper GPT-5.5 looks only a few points above 5.4 — but that's because 5.5 is far more efficient with its thinking. Once you control for thinking time/compute, 5.5 is a substantial jump over 5.4. Why not just let 5.5 think as long as 5.4? Because the point at which modern…
featured.insightZh: 现代模型的能力是「你往里砸多少钱」的函数，而所有人还在用一个不控制 test-time compute（测试时算力）的单数字基准表来评估它们——这套评估方式从根上就错了。 No Priors 这期请来 OpenAI 研究科学家、AI 推理（reasoning）领域的「教父」之一 Noam Brown。他的核心论点针对的是那张所有人发新模型时都会贴的「基准表格」（x 轴一堆 benchmark、y 轴各模型分数）。问题在于：这张表用单个数字代表一个模型在一个基准上的表现，却不控制每道题用了多少 test-time compute。GPT-5.5 在纸面上只比 5.4 高几个百分点，看着像挤牙膏，但真正原因是 5.5「思考」效率高得多——一旦你把思考时间/算力拉平来比，5.5 是对 5.4 的实质性跃升。 为什么不干脆让 5.5 思考得和 5.4 一样久？因为现代模型「性能触顶」的那个点已经远到没法测了。Brown 说，如果脚手架搭得合理，5.5 这类模型能持续高效思考数周，触顶点远在可测范围之外。所以他主张评估方式必须改：要么给基准设定 token/成本/时间预算，要么把性能画成「test-time compute 的函数」曲线，这样模型之间才好比。 这个观点有个「不方便的真相」版本延伸到安全评估上：各家实验室的「负责任扩展政策 / 准备度框架」大多是在 ChatGPT 时代（test-time compute scaling 还不成气候时）设计的，根本没考虑「该在什么算力预算下评估模型的危险能力」。如果一个模型在 1 万美元预算下能做的事远超 10 美元预算，那评估它能否被用来造生化武器时，到底该用哪个预算？现行政策回避了这个问题。Brown 直言：「我们只是在假装这个问题不存在。」他还泼了盆冷水：他不认为会发生「一夜之间智能爆炸」式的快速起飞，因为模型解锁最强能力高度依赖大规模 test-time compute，而这本质上被时间卡住——「时间本身成了瓶颈」，这也是所有前沿实验室研究员现在如此玩命工作的原因。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Y Combinator president and CEO Garry Tan didn't mince words about the gated release: "This is honestly no way to release a model and continued development and release this way is a solid way to salt the ground and kill all innovation by small startups." From the YC seat, his worry is that gating frontier models directly chokes off independent builders and early-stage founders. His other widely-shared note this week: don't be a mid startup — harsh, but true.
items.insightZh: Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 对 GPT-5.6 这种「限制访问」的发布方式毫不留情：「老实说这根本不是发布模型的方式，照这样继续开发和发布，是给土地撒盐、扼杀所有小创业公司创新的稳妥做法。」站在 YC 立场，他担心前沿模型门槛化会直接掐死独立 builder 和早期创业者的生存空间。他另一条广为流传的提醒是：别做一个平庸的创业公司——这话听着扎心但是真的。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper turned the GPT-5.6 Sol gating into an opinionated "BREAKING" post. Per a US government directive, access is currently limited to ~20 pre-approved companies, and Every isn't on the list. He applauds the need for some oversight on cyber resilience, but argues that widespread democratic access to frontier models is essential to America's lead in the AI race and to letting workers keep pace. His underrated point: early testers like Every lose the ability to prepare people for these tools if they…
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 把 GPT-5.6 Sol 的访问限制写成了一篇带立场的「BREAKING」。按美国政府指令，访问目前限于约 20 家预批准公司，Every 不在名单上——他理解政府在网络安全等层面做监督的必要，但强烈认为「让前沿模型广泛、民主化地可用」对美国在 AI 竞赛中的领先地位绝对必要，也是让美国劳动者跟上新技能的关键。他点出一个被低估的连带损失：像 Every 这样的早期测试者一旦失去访问，就失去了「提前测试、帮美国人学会用好这些工具」的能力。好在 OpenAI 和政府似乎都在推动尽快放开。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch dug into why agents are notoriously hard-to-debug software, on two levels: by design, AI models are non-deterministic — even two identical prompts don't always yield the same output; and agents are also complex distributed systems, with multi-step computation across functions and sandboxes, touching dozens of API services that go down or rate-limit you. That's why nailing observability out of the box was a key team priority. He also dropped a design-world verdict: "The UI for AI is here.…
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 这周聊的是 agent 为什么是出了名地难调试，本质有两层：一是设计使然——AI 模型行为非确定，同样的两个 prompt 都不一定给出相同输出；二是 agent 本身就是复杂的分布式系统，跨函数、跨 sandbox 的多步计算，触达几十个随时可能宕机或限流的 API 服务。所以他说 Vercel 把「开箱即用的可观测性」当成了团队的关键优先级。他还甩出一句对设计圈的判断：「AI 的 UI 已经到了，就是 shadcn。」

items.title: Nan Yu · Linear 产品负责人
items.summaryEn: Linear's head of product Nan Yu shared a sharp framing on problem triage he calls "secret level 6": there's a problem, but it's not worth solving, so leave it alone. His argument: this is exactly why an org full of "level 1s" can win — they don't get distracted by side quests. In a world where everyone wants to flex high-level problem-solving, knowing which problems to deliberately not solve is its own scarce judgment.
items.insightZh: Linear 产品负责人 Nan Yu 分享了一个关于「问题分级」的洞察，他称之为「秘密的第 6 级」：有个问题存在，但不值得解决，所以就放着别管。他的论点是——这正是为什么一个充满「第 1 级」执行者的组织能赢：他们不会被支线任务分心。在人人都想展示「高阶解决能力」的环境里，知道哪些问题该故意不解决，本身就是一种稀缺判断力。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari fired a shot at the endless "taste" discourse: the funniest part is that a lot of the commentary comes from people who never built anything — you can't achieve or refine taste without being in the arena. His chef analogy: nobody expects your first dish to be great, but after 100 iterations and 100 dishes, the 101st has imbued all the lessons from 10,000 iterations. Over-fit without variation, though, and people get bored — the best learn, imbue, and innovate by consistently brea…
items.insightZh: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 对当下满天飞的「taste（品味）」讨论开了一炮：最讽刺的是，大量评论 taste 的人自己从没做过任何东西——你不下场就练不出（也修不出）taste。他用厨师做比方：没人指望第一道菜就惊艳，但做了 100 次、100 道菜之后，第 101 道菜里浸透了那 1 万次迭代的全部教训。但若是缺乏变化地过拟合，人们又会腻——最好的人能在持续打破模式中学习、内化、创新。他还抛出一个反主流判断：跟大多数人不同，他认为 AI 真有机会练出自己的 taste。

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · South Park Commons 合伙人、前 Dropbox CTO
items.summaryEn: South Park Commons partner and former Dropbox CTO Aditya Agarwal named an interesting side effect of AI: he now has zero tolerance for shallow interactions with humans. What he craves is real depth in relationships, and more ways to get there are hugely valuable; for everything else, give him agents. He predicts our world becomes both smaller and richer in relationship depth.
items.insightZh: South Park Commons 合伙人、前 Dropbox CTO Aditya Agarwal 讲了 AI 的一个有趣副作用：他对与人的浅层互动已经零容忍。他真正渴望的是关系里的深度连接，而能加深这种连接的方式都极其宝贵；至于其他一切——交给 agent 就好。他预测我们的世界会同时变得「更小」也「在关系深度上更丰富」。

items.title: Sam Altman · OpenAI CEO
items.summaryEn: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's updates this week centered on models and quotas: the team "cooked, spicily," and while it's "not quite all-you-can-eat tokens" yet, they're working on it. He also noted ChatGPT's 5.5 instant model got updated this week — "I like its vibes." Amid the GPT-5.6 gating controversy, these low-key updates quietly stoke expectations that access and quotas will eventually loosen.
items.insightZh: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 这周的几条更新都围绕模型与额度：他说团队「这次做得很辣（spicily）」，并预告虽然还不是「随便吃到饱的 token」，但正在朝那个方向努力。另外他提到本周更新了 ChatGPT 里用的 5.5 instant 模型——「我喜欢它的 vibe。」在 GPT-5.6 限制访问引发争议的当口，这些轻描淡写的更新某种程度上是在给「访问与额度终将放开」的预期添柴。

items.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI（Codex & ChatGPT）
items.summaryEn: OpenAI's Codex & ChatGPT lead Thibault Sottiaux announced a free usage reset for all Codex users, landing in accounts within hours. He clarified some mitigations were applied but the investigation hadn't shown users impacted at large, and the team keeps monitoring. The post drew heavy engineer attention (4,000+ likes) — a classic "give users their quota back first, run down root cause after" reassurance move.
items.insightZh: OpenAI 的 Codex & ChatGPT 负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 宣布给所有 Codex 用户「免费送一次额度重置」，几小时内到账。他同时说明已经上了一些缓解措施，但调查没有显示用户被大规模影响，团队会持续监控。这条在工程师圈引发大量关注（4000+ 赞），是典型的「先把用户额度还回去、再慢慢查根因」式快速安抚动作。

items.title: Cat Wu · Anthropic（Claude Code）
items.summaryEn: Cat Wu, who works on Claude Code + Cowork at Anthropic, plugged one of her favorite Claude Code on desktop features: split screen. A small feature that hits the real workflow of watching an agent work while you operate alongside it.
items.insightZh: Anthropic 做 Claude Code + Cowork 的 Cat Wu 安利了桌面版 Claude Code 的一个她最爱的功能：分屏（split screen）。小功能但戳中了「一边看 agent 干活、一边自己操作」的实际工作流痛点。

items.title: Swyx · Latent Space / AI Engineer 创始人
items.summaryEn: Latent Space and AI Engineer founder Swyx reported a swyx inc milestone: he took over a new media lab in San Francisco — a home for engineer-creatives, a third place to make, a finishing school for technical storytellers. Surprise bonus: it came with a randomly wired datacenter rack, and he's crowdsourcing ideas for what to put in it. He also ran a first-ever AI FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer) miniconference with Basil, noting that with both OpenAI and Anthropic launching multi-billion-dollar services arms, FDE is…
items.insightZh: Latent Space 与 AI Engineer 的创始人 Swyx 这周报告了 swyx inc 的一个里程碑：他在旧金山接手了一个新的 media lab，定位是「engineer-creatives 的新家、一个用来创造的第三空间、技术叙事者的进修学校」。意外的是这地方还自带了一个随机布好线的数据中心机架，他公开求建议该往里塞什么。另外他还和 Basil 一起办了首届 AI FDE（Forward Deployed Engineer）小型会议——他点出随着 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都推出数十亿美元的服务部门，FDE 已成为地球上最抢手的岗位之一。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder、Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Builder and Follow Builders author Zara Zhang plugged a badly underrated video recording/editing tool called Borumi — she describes it as "Screen Studio + Descript + CapCut all in one," so under-the-radar it doesn't even have an X account to tag. She also reshared a line that fit her vibe: "You do not need God to write your emails."
items.insightZh: Builder、Follow Builders 这套 skill 的作者 Zara Zhang 这周安利了一个被严重低估的视频录制/剪辑工具 Borumi——她形容它像「Screen Studio + Descript + CapCut 三合一」，低调到连个能 @ 的 X 账号都没有。她还转了一句很对她胃口的话：「你不需要上帝来帮你写邮件。」

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI
items.summaryEn: OpenClaw's Peter Steinberger vented about a developer perennial — Apple notarization: "I love how Apple notarization breaks multiple times a year until I manually log in and accept some new legal agreements." A relatable developer-life gripe; the ~1,000 likes say plenty of people share the pain.
items.insightZh: OpenClaw 的 Peter Steinberger 吐槽了开发者的老朋友——Apple 公证（notarization）：「我爱死了 Apple 公证一年要坏好几次，直到我手动登录、接受一些新的法律协议为止。」一条扎心的开发者日常，近千赞说明踩同款坑的人不在少数。
